label: CDN Management Pro
summary: Advanced multi-site CDN/edge orchestration with provider-qualified delivery profiles, origin/DNS binding, cache rules, purge workflows, TLS review and source-attributed cache/availability observations. Specific CDN providers remain connectors and retain their actual capability limits.
core_boundary: Core domain/DNS/TLS authority, ordinary caching/compression, origin security and essential hosting remain free. The current Nginx -> Apache -> FPM target routes all content, including static files, through Apache with edge direct-file/response-cache off by default. This module adds advanced CDN policy coordination only; no protected/private response may move to an edge cache without explicitly admitted, versioned semantics, and no proprietary edge service becomes necessary for Core hosting or recovery.
acceptance: Bind each zone/distribution/profile to the authorized tenant, domain, origin, selected provider account and current resource revision before requesting an edge change.
Qualify origin TLS, certificate/hostname validation, SNI, origin authentication, direct-origin exposure policy and management-recovery access without disabling mandatory checks.

Review cache keys for Host/tenant/resource, query and negotiated variants, including Vary/Accept-Encoding; require bypass for logged-in users, authorization headers, sessions, carts, admin/private APIs, cookies, private responses and state-changing methods to prevent poisoning or cross-account disclosure.

Preserve all-request Apache authorization in the current Nginx -> Apache -> FPM target: default edge-cache/direct-file remains disabled, including for CSS/assets protected by nested .htaccess or directory access rules.

Require explicit Core-owner admission/versioning and negative protected-file/auth/cookie/private-content tests before any CDN cache policy or authority handoff; compression and CDN connectivity do not authorize public caching.

Qualify compression negotiation, variant isolation, double-compression prevention, effective resource budgets and supported rollback. Secret-bearing dynamic compression requires its own risk/correctness decision and must remain bypassed when unqualified.
Implement bounded scoped purge/invalidation with provider receipts, replay handling and explicit propagation uncertainty; acceptance is not global purge completion.
Constrain rewrites, redirects, upstream destinations, compression and edge-worker features to admitted capabilities and separately reviewed code where applicable.
Measure cache correctness, origin/offload behavior, stale responses, error rates and request costs for each provider/profile; avoid treating CDN activation as proof of faster or safer delivery.
Exercise provider outage, credential rotation/revocation, DNS/certificate changes and failed deployments with a documented service-specific exit/recovery path.
Disabling premium orchestration must preserve current delivery policy and independent Core origin/DNS/TLS control; provider removal requires dependency review rather than silently breaking sites.
